Class Inventory

java.lang.Object
Inventory
public class Inventory extends Object
This class represents an inventory for storing electronic devices. It manages the addition, removal, update, listing, sorting, calculation of total value, restocking, and exporting of inventory reports.

    • linkedList

      private LinkedList<ArrayList<Device>> linkedList
      Linked list containing array lists of devices. Each node of the linked list holds an array list containing devices of a specific category.

  • Constructor Details

    • Inventory

      public Inventory()
      Constructs a new Inventory object with an empty linked list. The linked list will be used to store array lists of devices, with each node representing a different category of devices.

  • Method Details

    • addDevice

      public void addDevice()
      Adds a new device to the inventory. Time complexity: O(1).

    • removeDevice

      public void removeDevice(String deviceName)
      Removes the device with the specified name from the inventory. If a device with the given name is found, it is removed from the inventory. Only the first occurrence of the device with the specified name is removed.
      Parameters:
      deviceName - the name of the device to be removed Time complexity: O(m*n) = O(5n) = O(n), where 'n' is the total number of devices and 'm' is the maximum number of device categories (which is 5 in this case).

    • updateStock

      public void updateStock(String deviceName)
      Updates the stock details (price and quantity) of a device with the specified name in the inventory. If a device with the given name is found, the user is prompted to enter new price and quantity values. The device's price and quantity are updated accordingly. If the user leaves the input blank for price or quantity, the current values are retained.
      Parameters:
      deviceName - - the name of the device to be updated Time complexity: O(m*n) = O(5n) = O(n), where 'n' is the total number of devices and 'm' is the maximum number of device categories (which is 5 in this case).

    • displayDevices

      public void displayDevices()
      Displays the details of all devices in the inventory. It iterates through the array lists containing devices of different categories and prints the details of each device, including category, name, price, and quantity. Time complexity: O(m*n) = O(5n) = O(n), where 'n' is the total number of devices and 'm' is the maximum number of device categories (which is 5 in this case).

    • cheapestDevice

      public void cheapestDevice()
      Finds and displays the details of the cheapest device in the inventory. It iterates through the array lists containing devices of different categories and compares the price of each device to find the cheapest one. If the inventory is empty, it prints a message indicating that there are no devices in the inventory. Time complexity: O(m*n) = O(5n) = O(n), where 'n' is the total number of devices and 'm' is the maximum number of device categories (which is 5 in this case).
      See Also:
      • Device

    • sortArrayListAndDisplay

      public void sortArrayListAndDisplay()
      Sorts the devices within each ArrayList in the linked list by their prices in ascending order using Java's built-in sorting algorithm and displays the sorted devices. Time complexity: O(nlogn), where 'n' is the total number of devices in all ArrayLists. The sorting algorithm used is Timsort, which has an average time complexity of O(nlogn).

    • calculateTotalPrice

      public double calculateTotalPrice()
      Calculates the total price of all devices in the inventory by summing the product of each device's price and quantity. Time complexity: O(n), where 'n' is the total number of devices in all ArrayLists. This method iterates through all devices in the inventory once to calculate the total price.
      Returns:
      The total price of all devices in the inventory.

    • restockDevice

      public void restockDevice(String deviceName, int newQuantity, boolean action)
      Restocks or removes stock for a device in the inventory based on the specified parameters. Time complexity: O(n), where 'n' is the total number of devices in all ArrayLists. This method iterates through all devices in the inventory to find the device with the specified name.
      Parameters:
      deviceName - The name of the device to restock or remove.
      newQuantity - The quantity to add or remove from the device's stock.
      action - A boolean value indicating whether to add (true) or remove (false) the specified quantity.

    • exportInventoryReport

      public void exportInventoryReport()
      It writes the informations about the devices into the file. Time complexity: O(m*n) = O(5n) = O(n) m can be maximum 5. The code has fixed Device number.
